mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact lets a Member who is not the task's owner succeed at PATCH/DELETE; the injected fact constructs exactly such a Success op (non-owner, role=Member), which the OwnershipBasedAccess predicate is supposed to forbid.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OwnershipBypass { some op: Operation, t: Task, m: Membership | op.kind = PatchTask and op.outcome = Success and op.target = t and m.user = op.caller and m.team = op.teamCtx and m.role = Member and op.caller != t.owner }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows a Success operation to act on a task whose team differs from the caller's X-Team-Id. The injection forces such an instance — a clear cross-team leak that NoInformationLeakage must catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CrossTeamLeak { some op: Operation, t: Task, m: Membership | op.outcome = Success and op.kind = GetTaskById and op.target = t and m.user = op.caller and m.team = op.teamCtx and t.team != op.teamCtx }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the matrix definition lets PermMatrix.Allowed be anything. The injection collapses it to empty, so PermissionCompleteness (every Role x OperationKind cell present) fails.
Without this fact, a successful PATCH need not produce an audit entry. The injection forces a PATCH-Success op with writesAudit empty, which AuditCompleteness must reject.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditMissing { some op: Operation, t: Task, m: Membership | op.outcome = Success and op.kind = PatchTask and op.target = t and m.user = op.caller and m.team = op.teamCtx and m.role = Admin and no op.writesAudit }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact lets an audit entry's kind diverge from its producing operation's kind — e.g., a PostTasks op producing a DeletedKind entry, which is impossible under an append-only invariant where the kind is fixed at insert time.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditKindMismatch { some op: Operation, a: AuditEntry | op.writesAudit = a and op.kind = PostTasks and a.kind = DeletedKind }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact lets an audit entry's actor differ from the caller of the producing operation — misattribution. The injection forces such a mismatch, which AttributionCorrectness must detect.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_Misattribution { some op: Operation, a: AuditEntry | op.writesAudit = a and a.actor != op.caller }
